title: How 100+ Unit Vacation Rental Property Managers Automate Bookkeeping
summary: Learn the bookkeeping automation systems 100+ unit vacation rental managers use to eliminate manual work and scale without adding finance staff.
body_text: Vacation rental operators managing 100+ units don't rely on spreadsheets or massive finance teams—they build integrated automation systems. By implementing financial automation platforms that connect their PMS, banking, and expenses, they eliminate 85-90% of manual bookkeeping work while maintaining proper trust accounting. This documented playbook lets one employee manage 300+ units efficiently. Most vacation rental operators hit a wall around 25 units. The spreadsheets that worked fine at 10 doors suddenly can't keep up. Reconciliation consumes entire weekends. Owner statements take longer to prepare. You're spending more time in QuickBooks than talking to guests or owners. This is the moment that separates operators who stall from those who scale cleanly to 100, 200, even 500 units. The successful ones understand early that bookkeeping can become a major bottleneck if you don't solve for it proactively. It only consumes more of your time as you grow. So they solve for growth pains early on and use the time they get back to focus on expanding their portfolio and keeping owners happy. This article breaks down the specific systems that let elite vacation rental managers automate their bookkeeping operations without sacrificing accuracy, compliance, or control. What 100 Units Actually Means for Your Books Before diving into automation, it helps to understand what you're managing at scale. A 100-unit vacation rental portfolio creates operational complexity that traditional accounting systems simply can't handle: 3,000-4,000 monthly transactions across Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, and direct bookings—every payout, fee deduction, guest charge, refund, and adjustment needs proper recording and categorization 100+ individual owner P&Ls that require separate tracking and reporting—you can't aggregate portfolio performance because each owner needs precise visibility into their specific property's revenue, expenses, and profitability 15-25 active vendors with varying billing cycles, payment terms, and methods—some invoice monthly, others charge cards immediately, and tracking who's been paid and which expenses belong to which properties becomes its own administrative challenge Multiple bank accounts managing trust funds, operating capital, and owner reserves—proper trust accounting demands strict separation of owner funds from operating expenses, with clear audit trails for every dollar Platform-specific payout structures that don't align with standard accounting periods—Airbnb pays differently than Vrbo, which pays differently than Booking.com, and reconciling these variations manually consumes hours weekly This complexity is what breaks manual bookkeeping systems. Not because operators lack skill or diligence, but because the architecture itself can't support this volume and variability without collapsing under its own weight. What Month-End Actually Looks Like Today The pain of manual bookkeeping becomes most obvious during month-end close. For most 100-unit operations running manual processes, this spans 5-7 work days and involves coordinating between multiple team members—bookkeepers, accountants, operations staff. You're reconciling multiple bank accounts against platform payouts that don't match cleanly. You're coding hundreds of credit card transactions and expenses to properties and GL accounts—trying to remember which Home Depot charge was for which property, which cleaning supply order belongs where. You're chasing down your maintenance team for missing receipts from three weeks ago because without that documentation, you can't bill the expense back to owners. You're processing expense reports submitted late by team members, often discovering purchases that should have been owner-reimbursable but weren't properly tracked. You're entering vendor bills one by one. You're cross-checking reimbursable expenses against what actually got billed to owners, often discovering gaps where revenue was lost because someone forgot to flag an expense or a receipt went missing. Then comes owner statement preparation—pulling finalized revenue and expense data, calculating owner distributions using complex spreadsheet formulas, formatting statements individually, reviewing everything for obvious errors, and sending via email. Then you immediately start fielding questions from owners who notice discrepancies or want clarifications. The emotional cost is significant: high anxiety, weekend work, relationship strain with both team members and owners. And this process doesn't improve as you add more properties—it gets worse. This is why at 25-50 units, most operators hire part-time bookkeepers or engage third-party accounting firms. Beyond 50 units, that becomes a full-time bookkeeper costing $60,000-$80,000 annually or even higher retainers to accounting firms. At 300 units, you're looking at 2-3 full-time bookkeepers. At 500 units, traditional operations require a dedicated finance team. But there's a different path. The Critical Infrastructure Shift What most operators get wrong about automation is looking for tools that make individual tasks faster—better receipt scanners, smarter spreadsheets, more efficient reconciliation software. But operators managing 100+ units learned something different. What you actually need is a financial automation platform that sits between your PMS and your accounting software, becoming your single source of truth. Think of it as a reconciliation and verification layer. Your PMS captures reservation data. Your bank processes actual transactions. Your accounting software maintains your general ledger. But none of these systems talk to each other natively, and none of them understand vacation rental operations specifically. A specialized financial automation platform connects all three, reconciling data from each side and maintaining the authoritative record of what actually happened financially. This is how you eliminate the constant manual data transfers that consume 15-20 hours weekly in traditional operations. The Foundation: Connecting Your Operations to Your Books The transformation starts with two critical integrations that create a continuous data flow between your operational systems and your financial records. This is what a financial automation platform actually does—it sits between your property management system and your accounting software, translating operational activity into accurate financial records. PMS Integration: Pulling Operational Data Automatically A financial automation platform integrates natively with leading property management systems—Guesty, Hostaway, Streamline, OwnerRez, Track, Hostfully, Hospitable, and Feather—to pull reservation data, payout information, and property details automatically. When a guest books through Airbnb, your PMS captures it automatically. The financial automation platform receives that data in real-time, calculates the expected net payout after platform fees, and creates properly coded revenue entries for the correct property and owner—all without CSV downloads or manual data entry. This connection eliminates 10-15 hours of weekly reconciliation work. Accounting Software Integration: Syncing to Your General Ledger On the other side, the financial automation platform connects directly to your accounting software—QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, Xero, or Sage Intacct—pushing properly categorized transactions and maintaining your chart of accounts without manual journal entries. All the reconciled data from your PMS, your banking transactions, your expenses, and your vendor payments flows automatically into your accounting system with proper coding. Property-level P&Ls update in real-time. Trust accounting entries post correctly. Owner distributions record accurately. Your CPA or tax preparer gets clean books without you spending hours exporting data, reformatting spreadsheets, or manually posting journal entries. The financial automation platform handles the translation between vacation rental operations and proper accounting standards. The Advanced Capabilities That Transform Operations While connecting your PMS to your accounting software is foundational, the real transformation comes from additional automation capabilities that most basic integrations don't offer. The most sophisticated financial automation platforms—like Topkey—add critical functions that turn month-end from a 5-7 day ordeal into a 1-2 day process with better accuracy and zero revenue leakage. Smart Corporate Cards for Expense Management Expense tracking destroys most manual operations. Your maintenance team buys supplies without saving receipts. Cleaning coordinators submit expense reports weeks late. Purchases get coded to wrong properties. Reimbursable expenses that should be billed to owners slip through entirely. Advanced platforms solve this with intelligent corporate card capabilities that work with both platform-issued cards and your existing high-earning business cards—letting you keep your favorite rewards while adding automation. Every card swipe triggers instant alerts, giving you complete visibility and control over property-level expenses and owner billables as they happen. Employees can upload or forward receipts in seconds via email or mobile app. AI automatically matches receipts to the correct transaction, property, and GL code. No more chasing down your team for documentation. Instead of relying on delayed or failed bank feeds, direct card connections provide instant transaction data with AI-powered GL coding that categorizes expenses automatically. When your maintenance coordinator swipes a card at Home Depot for $347, the transaction appears immediately. The system recognizes Home Depot as a maintenance vendor, suggests "Repairs & Maintenance" as the category, prompts for property assignment, and flags it as owner-reimbursable if applicable. For 100-unit portfolios, this typically eliminates 8-12 hours of monthly work while recovering $2,000 to $5,000 monthly in previously missed reimbursable expenses. That's $24,000 to $60,000 annually in revenue that may have been contractually yours. Automated Bill Pay Vendor payment management becomes unworkable at scale when done manually. You're tracking invoices from 15-25 vendors with different billing cycles, payment terms, and delivery methods. Some want checks, others prefer ACH, some charge credit cards directly. Sophisticated platforms centralize bill pay with approval workflows built in. Invoices get uploaded or emailed directly into the system. They're automatically matched to vendors and coded to properties. Approval routing ensures the right people review expenses before payment. Once approved, payments process automatically via ACH, check, or card—whatever the vendor prefers. This eliminates the chaos of tracking what's been paid, what's outstanding, and which expenses belong to which properties. More importantly, it ensures vendors get paid on time, protecting critical relationships with maintenance teams, cleaners, and service providers. Invoicing and Reimbursements Beyond tracking expenses, you need to bill owners for reimbursable costs and invoice clients for management fees or services rendered. Manual invoicing means creating documents individually, tracking payment status in spreadsheets, and following up on overdue accounts. Advanced automation handles this seamlessly . Owner-reimbursable expenses captured via corporate cards flow directly into invoices. Management fees calculate based on pre-set rules. Invoices generate and send automatically. Payment tracking happens in real-time, and overdue notices trigger without manual intervention. For property managers handling reimbursements to team members or contractors, the platform streamlines that process as well—capturing the expense, routing for approval, and processing payment without the typical administrative burden. Revenue Reconciliation Across Platforms This might be the most critical function for vacation rental operators . You're collecting revenue from Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, direct bookings, and payment processors like Stripe—each with different payout structures, fee calculations, and timing. Manually reconciling these against bank deposits and PMS records can consume 10-15 hours weekly. Advanced platforms automate revenue reconciliation by connecting directly to booking platforms, your PMS, payment processors, and your bank to match every dollar to its corresponding reservation. Instead of trying to match bulk deposits to individual bookings manually, the system breaks down platform payouts into individual reservations automatically. Every booking dollar gets matched to its corresponding reservation, giving you precise, review-ready revenue numbers without spreadsheets or manual matching. Direct integrations with major OTAs—particularly Airbnb—ensure accurate payout reconciliation without scraping, browser extensions, or manual CSV exports. The system automatically reconciles what matches cleanly while surfacing underpayments, overpayments, and unmatched revenue that needs your attention. Once funds are matched and reconciled, they're automatically allocated to the correct owner's trust account based on the reconciled revenue. This reduces manual handling, minimizes allocation errors, and supports proper trust accounting workflows—critical for protecting your business from compliance violations. By pulling data directly from OTAs, Stripe, your PMS, and your bank, sophisticated platforms centralize and reconcile revenue data automatically. No more piecing together reports across multiple systems, dealing with error-prone spreadsheets, or manually deduplicating transactions. This continuous revenue reconciliation allows operators to trust their numbers at any moment—not just after spending days on month-end reconciliation work. The Outcome: Transformed Month-End Close When these integrations and automation functions work together, month-end close transforms completely. With proper automation, month-end close becomes a 1-2 day process managed by a single person. Revenue is reconciled continuously through automated platform monitoring. Expenses are coded automatically through smart cards and bill pay. Invoices and reimbursements are processed throughout the month. You're not compiling data from multiple sources—it's consolidated and reconciled in real-time. Instead of spending 5-7 days coordinating across multiple people, you're spending 1-2 days reviewing consolidated data, catching the handful of exceptions that need investigation, and generating owner statements. The heavy lifting happens automatically in the background throughout the month. More importantly, the output becomes more accurate because you've eliminated most manual data handling where errors occur. Owners stop asking clarifying questions because numbers reconcile properly month after month. The Compliance Factor That Changes Everything Here's what often gets overlooked in automation conversations: trust accounting compliance. Vacation rental operators hold other people's money. Owner reserves, security deposits, advance bookings—these aren't your funds, and proper accounting standards require strict separation and documentation. Mix these accounts improperly, and you're facing regulatory violations that could threaten your entire business. Manual systems struggle with this. Spreadsheets can't enforce trust accounting rules. Generic accounting software doesn't understand vacation rental fund flows. You're relying on human vigilance to catch mistakes before they become compliance issues. Purpose-built financial automation platforms handle trust accounting by design. They understand which transactions belong in trust accounts versus operating accounts. They maintain the required audit trails automatically. They ensure owner funds never get commingled with business expenses. This isn't just about efficiency—it's about protecting your business from the kind of compliance failures that destroy property management companies. The Real Financial Impact Beyond time savings, automation creates value in three measurable categories: Labor cost avoidance: Traditional bookkeeping scales predictably and expensively. At 25-50 units, you're hiring part-time help or paying accounting firms thousands monthly. Beyond 50 units, that's a full-time bookkeeper at $60,000-$80,000 annually. At 300 units, you need 2-3 bookkeepers costing $120,000-$240,000 annually. With financial automation platforms, one person can manage 400-500 units comfortably. At 300 units, that's $40,000 to $180,000 in avoided annual labor costs. At 500 units, you're avoiding $20,000 to $260,000 annually. Revenue recovery: Manual operations often miss reimbursable expenses. For 100-unit portfolios, automated systems can recover $2,000-$5,000 monthly in previously missed charges—$24,000 to $60,000 annually in revenue you were entitled to bill. Risk reduction: Automated systems with proper controls dramatically reduce compliance risk, audit exposure, and owner disputes stemming from inaccurate statements. The value of avoiding a single trust accounting violation far exceeds infrastructure costs. Making the Transition The most common concern about automation is implementation complexity. Operators worry about disrupting current operations or losing data during migration. The reality is much simpler than most expect: Day 1: Connect Everything Your financial automation platform connects to your PMS and accounting software. The foundational integrations go live immediately, establishing the data flow between your operational systems and financial records. Weeks 1-2: Team Training Your full team—accountants, general managers, field staff—learns the new workflows. Training covers expense card usage, receipt submission, approval processes, and how to access real-time financial data. Parallel processing ensures accuracy as everyone adapts. Week 2: Platform Fully Operational Workflows are in place and functioning. Automated reconciliation, expense coding, and revenue matching are working smoothly. Results start showing immediately—cleaner data, faster processing, fewer manual tasks. Month 1: Complete Integration You're fully operational with all automation functions active. Your first automated month-end close reveals the transformation—what used to take 5-7 days with multiple people now takes 1-2 days with one person. The critical decision is choosing a financial automation platform that actually understands vacation rental operations. Generic accounting software doesn't handle multi-platform revenue, property-level P&Ls, or trust accounting requirements. You need specialized infrastructure built specifically for STR operations. CPAs and tax preparers strongly prefer working with automated systems. Transaction data is categorized consistently, supporting documentation is attached digitally, and trust accounting compliance is built-in. Year-end tax preparation becomes faster and more accurate, often reducing accounting fees during tax season. Why Infrastructure Beats Effort At 25 units, you can still power through with manual processes and long hours. At 50 units, you're hiring help just to keep up. At 100 units, manual operations require multiple full-time positions constantly fighting to maintain accuracy—and despite all that effort, mistakes are inevitable. When bookkeeping relies on tedious manual tasks like matching transactions in spreadsheets, coding expenses by hand, and chasing receipts, human error becomes a question of when, not if. The operators who successfully scale past these thresholds recognized one truth early: throwing more labor at bookkeeping problems doesn't solve the underlying infrastructure gap. It just makes the problem more expensive. Financial automation platforms don't help you do the same work faster. They eliminate entire categories of manual work that shouldn't exist in modern operations. When your PMS connects directly to specialized financial infrastructure, when expenses get captured automatically at the source, when revenue reconciles continuously, and when owner data consolidates in real-time, you're not working smarter—you're working fundamentally differently. This is how one finance person manages 400-500 units. Not through exceptional talent or superhuman effort, but through infrastructure that handles complexity automatically in the background. The question facing property managers isn't whether this approach works—it's whether manual operations can survive at scale at all. And increasingly, the answer is no. With native integrations to Guesty, Hostaway, Streamline, OwnerRez, Track, Hostfully, Hospitable, and Feather, plus connections to QuickBooks Online, NetSuite, Xero, and Sage Intacct, Topkey gives you the complete financial infrastructure to scale efficiently. ‍ Book a demo to see how operators are eliminating 85-90% of manual bookkeeping work while maintaining proper trust accounting standards.

title: Your 4-Week Leg Waxing Schedule for Smooth Results
summary: Discover why a 4-week leg waxing schedule keeps your skin smoother for longer. Get tips, pro advice, and a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader’s go-to exfoliation secret.
body_text: If you want smooth legs all the time, it’s not just about getting a wax — it’s about how often you wax. Timing makes a big difference. That’s why so many people stick to a 4-week leg waxing schedule. It’s long enough to let your hair grow just right for a clean removal and smooth finish, but not so long that you lose that soft, stubble-free feel in between. Let’s talk about why four weeks tends to be the sweet spot and how to make it work for you. Why Three to Four Weeks Hits the Sweet Spot Your hair grows in cycles. Some hairs are in active growth, some are in a state of rest, and others are in a transition phase. Your wax will last its longest when hair is removed during the active growth phase, since this is when the hair is most deeply rooted and full removal from the follicle is most likely. By sticking to a consistent leg waxing schedule over time, it’s easier to target hair during this phase. Most people find that leg hair is ready to wax again somewhere between three and four weeks. Three to four weeks gives enough time for all the hair to grow to the ideal length so the wax can grab it easily. Wait too long, and you risk less effective results. Go too soon, and some hairs may be too short to catch. How It Helps Your Skin Too Keeping a regular schedule means your hair starts growing in more evenly, so each wax gives you smoother, longer-lasting results. Over time, many people notice their hair feels finer and softer when it grows back. On the flip side: Wax too soon, and you risk missing those shorter hairs. Wait too long, and the service can feel a little less comfortable because the hair is longer. Inspiration from the Pros If anyone knows about keeping skin smooth, it’s the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders. In this Us Weekly feature on Kelly Villares , she talks about how regular visits to European Wax Center are a big part of her game-day routine. From legs to brows to Brazilians, she and her teammates keep a tight schedule so they’re always performance-ready. Kelly even shares her go-to product for keeping skin smooth between appointments: the EWC TREAT® Face & Body Exfoliating Gel . It uses natural fruit enzymes from papaya, pineapple, and lemon peel extract to gently loosen and remove dead skin cells without scrubbing, making it safe for both face and body. When used regularly on the legs, it helps keep hair follicles clear so new growth can come in smoothly, which means fewer bumps and longer-lasting results from each wax. Her routine is proof that when you stick to a plan, your legs stay ready without the stress of last-minute touch-ups. How to Make the Most of Your 4-Week Routine Here’s how to keep things simple between appointments: Before your wax: Let your hair grow to about the length of a grain of rice. Gently exfoliate the day before, and skip heavy lotions on the day of your appointment. After your wax: Give your skin a little breathing room. Wear loose clothing for the first 24 hours and avoid things like hot baths or heavy workouts that could irritate freshly waxed skin. Between visits: Exfoliate two or three times a week, moisturize daily, and keep an eye on your calendar so you stay close to your 4-week mark. Why Going Pro Makes a Difference Sure, you could try waxing at home, but having a Wax Specialist take care of it means the hair gets removed in the natural direction it grows, which helps avoid breakage and helps prevent ingrown hairs. It also results in smoother results, since getting all the hair yourself (especially on the backs of the thighs) can be tricky. Overall, it’s messier, more painful, and more time-consuming to do yourself. At EWC, we prep your skin before we even start, and provide a smooth service from start to finish. Keep the Smooth Going A 4-week schedule is easy to follow and helps you keep your legs looking and feeling their best all year long. Once you get into the rhythm, it becomes second nature. title: What to Expect at Mobile World Congress 2026
summary: What to Expect at Mobile World Congress 2026 Making sense of the hype, buzz, and excitement of MWC Barcelona 2026
body_text: Making sense of the hype, buzz, and excitement of MWC Barcelona 2026 The buzz is building as the telecom industry is gearing up for its biggest event of the year: Mobile World Congress (MWC). This year’s MWC is expected to draw more than 109,000 attendees, from operators and service providers to vendors, analysts, and innovators, all converging to showcase the technologies shaping our connected future. For one week, the spotlight turns to the ideas, partnerships, and breakthroughs that will define the next wave of innovation in telecom. As always, the show floor promises to be a spectacle. Innovation will be on full display, from humanoid robots and drones to IoT ecosystems, AI-powered smart glasses, electric vehicles, laptops with transparent displays, and more. Rumors are already swirling around potential device debuts, devices with advanced embedded AI capabilities, multi-spectral camera lenses, and a new range of wearables. Behind every headline-grabbing device, however, lies the real engine of innovation: the technology and infrastructure powering the industry. Here are some of the key themes set to take center stage at this year’s MWC: Agentic AI No doubt, this is this year’s biggest buzzword – agentic AI is rapidly reshaping network operations through intelligent, autonomous agents that monitor, optimize, and manage networks in real time. In the lead-up to the show, vendors and operators alike unveiled new agentic AI solutions, and at MWC, many will move beyond the hype to demonstrate these capabilities live on the show floor. According to Deloitte , Agentic AI represents a $150 billion opportunity for the telco industry, which is poised to fundamentally reimagine how operators design, run, and optimize their networks. As John McDermott, Global Telecom Leader, Deloitte Canada, said, “ Agentic AI is not just about technology—it’s about creating a strategic advantage, and telcos that act boldly will be the ones leading the charge. ” The industry’s AI direction is clear, but the road ahead is far from frictionless. MWC attendees can expect candid discussions about the operational and structural challenges that come with scaling AI across telecom networks. Beyond traffic growth, the industry must also confront mounting regulatory scrutiny, the challenge of scaling AI to meet escalating computational demands, rising energy consumption that could undermine both cost-efficiency and sustainability goals, and the operational challenges of implementing advanced AI-base use cases. The event will also highlight the challenges introduced by physical AI, i.e., systems that enable machines to perceive, interpret, and respond autonomously to real-world conditions. Physical AI presents a new set of challenges for telecom networks, shifting demands from predictable, human-centered traffic to real-time, autonomous, high-stakes workloads. Telecom operators sit at the very heart of this agentic AI adoption, and are uniquely positioned to enable it. These systems cannot function without deterministic, ultra-reliable network performance. Nor can they operate effectively without deep, real-time data and visibility into traffic flows and customer experience. As AI scales, it will redefine the telco’s role: from connectivity provider to AI-critical infrastructure partner. And network performance will no longer influence user experience alone. It will directly impact safety, operational continuity, and autonomous decision-making at scale. Native AI Agentic AI won’t be the only form of intelligence commanding attention at this year’s MWC. In 2026, Native AI is expected to move from concept to concrete architecture, signaling a transition from static “pipes” to autonomous, self-governing networks. Rather than layering AI on top of legacy systems, intelligence is being embedded directly into the network fabric, from RAN to core to edge. This is operationalizing AI at scale and fundamentally redefining how telecom infrastructure is built and managed. Key Native AI highlights at MWC: The rise of AI-native Radio Access Networks (AI-RAN), where neural models are embedded directly into silicon to optimize energy efficiency and performance in real time Autonomous mobile networks and closed-loop automation, with operators advancing toward Level 4 network autonomy by replacing manual workflows with AI-driven decision-making The evolution of “AI-as-a-Service,” powered by intent-based operations and infrastructure engineered to support real-time inference workloads at scale The development of AI-native internet architectures designed to handle the exponential surge in data and the ability to process it across distributed environments The shift is clearly moving from fragmented AI use cases toward fully integrated AI with self-optimizing networks that can dynamically adapt to changing traffic patterns, evolving service demands, and complex enterprise requirements. Ultimately, Native AI will no longer be positioned as an optional enhancement. It is emerging as the foundational design principle for next-generation telecom infrastructure, embedding the intelligence and native capabilities that future 6G networks will depend on. 6G Finally, while operators are still navigating the complexities of multi-cloud and hybrid environments and rolling out 5G standalone, the industry conversation is already turning to 6G. The accelerating AI supercycle, encompassing agentic, physical, and native AI and beyond, is placing a greater focus on 6G. While 5G was primarily optimized for content downloads, the rise of agentic AI flips this model, changing the equation by increasing the need for real-time, two-way data flows and smarter network management. And this is driving the adoption of adaptive, self-optimizing, AI-native architectures, enabling performance and reliability that 5G by itself was never built to deliver. These new AI systems require real-time interaction with the environment, demanding sub-millisecond latency and ultra-predictable, deterministic performance even under heavy network load. 3GPP has already begun laying the groundwork for 6G, running studies in parallel with the ongoing development of 5G Advanced specifications. At MWC, vendors, operators, and industry researchers are expected to spotlight next-generation infrastructure, including advanced antenna designs for 6G networks, ultra-high-speed data transfer technologies, and new spectrum in the 6–8 GHz range. These are all set to form the backbone of the future 6G ecosystem. Don’t Forget the Customer Experience Crucially, this year’s MWC will highlight that operators must embrace a fundamental shift, one that puts the customer at the center of every decision. Take Orange’s Trust the Future strategy, for example: by placing what it calls “customer intimacy” front and center and leveraging AI and digital technologies, it aims to enhance the customer experience while driving value, loyalty, and retention. Telecom operators are undoubtedly evolving into technology enablers, but even the most advanced networks and immersive innovations will fall short if the customer isn’t at the heart of every decision. With thousands of attendees at MWC, the companies that will truly stand out are those that can redefine the customer experience while optimizing network operations and delivering the agility needed to keep pace with a rapidly evolving digital landscape. RADCOM will be presenting the range of RADCOM ACE solutions, including the newly announced – RADCOM Neura, its AI Agent Suite designed for integration into agentic AI ecosystems. Along with the solutions presented, RADCOM will also showcase its High-Capacity User Analytics solution at MWC 2026. title: Centaur.ai Wins HealthAwards.com Gold for Mobile Digital Health Resources
summary: DiagnosUs has won the HealthAwards.com Gold award for Mobile Digital Health Resources, affirming its role as a leading platform for high-quality clinical data annotation. The recognition reinforces Centaur.ai’s accuracy-first approach, demonstrating that expert-validated labeling at scale is essential for trustworthy LLM training and evaluation in healthcare.
body_text: DiagnosUs wins Gold for Mobile Digital Health Resources ‍ Across the healthcare ecosystem, trust is earned when independent experts agree that a solution meaningfully improves clinical decision-making. This year, the Centaur.ai mobile application, DiagnosUs, notably received that validation. The Health Information Resource Center awarded DiagnosUs the HealthAwards.com Gold award for Mobile Digital Health Resources, selecting it from a field evaluated by a diverse panel of healthcare executives, clinicians, researchers, communications leaders, and digital health strategists. Their judgment spans every corner of modern healthcare, from major health systems and national associations to medical educators and payer-side professionals. An award grounded in that breadth of expertise signals something important. ‍ ‍ For Centaur.ai, it reinforces a principle we have stood by since the earliest days of our research at the MIT Center for Collective Intelligence: high-quality data annotation is the foundation on which reliable AI is built. The Gold award recognises DiagnosUs as a best-in-class mobile environment for real clinical problem solving. Still, its broader meaning lies in how it advances the quality and scale of training data for large models. ‍ Why this award matters for LLM data quality ‍ Training and evaluating healthcare-focused LLMs requires more than participation volume. It requires structured, diverse, and accuracy-first expertise, captured in a way that reflects real-world complexity. The HealthAwards.com judges assess solutions not only on usability but also on effectiveness, clinical relevance, and impact. Their recognition tells us that DiagnosUs is meeting a high bar for performance in environments where precision matters. ‍ That matters because DiagnosUs is not only a learning and assessment tool. It is one of the largest real-time pipelines for high-fidelity medical annotation worldwide. Every validated response inside the app strengthens the Centaur Network, which now includes clinicians, specialists, and trained community contributors working in a coordinated, quality-controlled system. The award highlights that this workflow is not theoretical. It is functional, measurable, and externally verified. ‍ ‍ Proof that a collective-intelligence model works at scale ‍ The HealthAwards.com Gold designation provides an independent confirmation of our central thesis: the best way to produce accurate labels for AI training and evaluation is to combine expert judgment with structured redundancy, targeted recruitment, and ongoing calibration. The judges evaluated DiagnosUs alongside clinical decision tools, patient-facing applications, and major digital health initiatives. Winning in that context signals that Centaur.ai has operationalized an accuracy-first approach that the broader industry recognizes as effective. ‍ This matters especially now. As LLMs take on more diagnostic, triage, summarization, and monitoring tasks, their performance depends directly on the quality of the data used to refine and evaluate them. Many models underperform not because of algorithmic limitations, but because the datasets behind them are noisy, inconsistent, or unrepresentative of clinical reality. DiagnosUs addresses this by transforming real medical judgment into structured, validated annotation events at scale. The Gold award is evidence that this system is producing measurable value. ‍ Why Centaur.ai is the quality leader in data annotation ‍ With DiagnosUs as its engine, Centaur.ai offers an annotation environment that meets the accuracy expectations of clinicians and the scalability expectations of modern AI developers. Clients rely on our platform for medical imaging, waveforms, clinical text, device data, robotics signals, and multimodal tasks where precision is non-negotiable. The award further validates that our pipeline is not only high-performing but also well-designed, trusted, and rigorous. ‍ In a moment when the market is saturated with annotation vendors promising speed above all else, an independently judged Gold award centered on quality is meaningful. It confirms that the Centaur model is uniquely equipped to deliver what healthcare AI truly needs: data accuracy at scale, validated by experts, and supported by a network that is continuously learning and improving. ‍ DiagnosUs earned this award. LLM developers reap the benefits. And the healthcare organizations deploying those models gain access to systems grounded in evidence rather than aspiration. body_text: Arqit quantum-safe keys now available pre-installed for Confidential Compute on Intel-based NetSec Cards February 24, 2026 9:00 am EST Download as PDF LONDON, Feb. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Arqit Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: ARQQ, ARQQW) (“Arqit”), a global leader in quantum-safe encryption, today announced the availability of its encryption software pre-installed inside an Intel Trust Domain Extensions (Intel TDX) trusted execution environment (TEE) on Intel NetSec Accelerator Reference Design-based accelerator cards. The result is confidential compute: trusted workloads, trusted networks, and trusted agents, even in shared or hostile environments. Interested customers can enable quantum-safe confidential computing by contacting Arqit . Intel TDX provides hardware‑enforced isolation of virtual machines (VMs) and containers to protect data during processing on 4th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processor and onwards. Arqit’s software generates quantum‑safe encryption keys which are created on demand and consumed within the TEE created by Intel TDX, separating workloads in multi-tenant environments and from cloud operators. The keys are never stored or exchanged, and Arqit’s cryptography provides security now and against future threats, even a quantum computer. Every data packet can now be protected with quantum-safe keys by default, at line speed, utilising hardware-accelerated technology, from cloud to edge. Enabling new high-growth security services for telecom operators and critical national infrastructure This development supports a wide range of telecom and critical communications infrastructure use cases, allowing service providers to deploy advanced security capabilities for existing and new offerings, including: Data sovereignty regardless of cloud or AI provider geography Quantum-safe data in transit and in process Secure Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) High-speed quantum safe IPSec VPNs without latency By embracing these capabilities, Telcos can differentiate their services and build new revenue streams while meeting the rising demand for post-quantum security and protecting ever more valuable digital assets by confidential computing across connected industries. “Your data already outlives your cryptography”, said Scott Alexander, Chief Product Officer at Arqit. “Regulators and customers expect crypto agility today; quantum-safe trust across confidential compute and edge networks is how you secure and future-proof your data and communications.” “Intel's market-leading security, built directly into our processors, provides the foundation for quantum-safe encryption in Arqit's solutions. Together, we are helping to establish unbreachable security as the standard for telco, government, and enterprise deployments,” said Cristina Rodriguez, VP and General Manager of Intel Network & Edge Group. Arqit and Intel will demonstrate this technology at MWC Barcelona 2026, replicating a customer’s on-prem environment and showcasing a cost-effective, efficient, and scalable confidential compute solution. Network security is no longer “fast encryption” – it is “fast and quantum-safe encryption”, reducing business risk.
